title: Unramified finite separable extensions of a discretely valued field are closed under subextension, Galois closure and compositum
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma has three parts for a discrete valuation ring A with fraction field K: that in a tower M/L/K of finite separable extensions, if M is unramified with respect to A then so is L; that any unramified finite separable L/K is contained in a Galois M/K that is unramified; and that two unramified finite separable extensions are contained in a common unramified finite separable extension (source lines 33066-33081). Part (1) argues with the integral closures C/B/A: since C is finite over B, Spec(C) -> Spec(B) is surjective, so every maximal ideal m of B has a maximal ideal m' of C above it; multiplicativity of ramification indices together with the hypothesis gives that the ramification index of B_m over A is 1, and since kappa(m')/kappa_A is finite separable the same holds for kappa(m)/kappa_A (proof lines 33089-33099). Part (2) identifies 'L unramified with respect to A' with 'A -> B is etale' where B is the integral closure, takes M to be the normal closure of L over K, uses the surjection from a tensor power of L over K onto M, and applies permanence of etale maps to conclude that the tensor power of B over A is etale over A, hence a product of Dedekind domains, so M is unramified (proof lines 33102-33127). Part (3) is carried out 'in the same manner' and the author states that the details are omitted (proof lines 33130-33132). The non-routine content is the identification of unramifiedness with etaleness for the integral closure and the use of permanence of etale maps to reach the normal closure.
